title: Global Affairs Canada -- digital transformation for women-led businesses, Benin
description:
"Minister Anand announced a total of approximately $17 million in funding for seven projects in Benin and across West Africa: $5 million to support women-led businesses through digital transformation; $4 million for a project to strengthen the leadership and empowerment of women and girls; approximately $1 million to develop and scale sustainable, inclusive, and locally sourced school meal supplies; $1.5 million to reduce gender disparities in West Africa's energy sector; $2 million for ordnance risk education and arms and ammunition management in border areas; $500,000 to strengthen regional border governance and security; and $3 million to advance international police cooperation in West Africa."

No implementing organisation is named for the digital-transformation line specifically; the other six lines in the same package are out of scope (not digitally specific) and are not recorded here.

title: Japan — Benin malaria AI/geospatial project (TICAD), 2026
description: "Benin launched a $2.3 million Japanese-funded project that will combine artificial intelligence, drones and geospatial mapping to strengthen malaria prevention in six pilot municipalities." "The government launched the Integrated Action for Malaria Prevention project in Cotonou on Tuesday, June 30. Japan is financing the initiative with $2.3 million." "Geospatial mapping tools and artificial intelligence will analyze environmental data to identify areas with the highest risk of mosquito breeding," with drones then used to spray WHO-approved larvicides.

title: Projet d'appui à la modernisation des systèmes d'information (PAMSI) de la DGI du Bénin
description:
PAMSI accompanies Benin's Direction générale des impôts in its digital transformation, to improve the tax administration's efficiency, ease taxpayer procedures and strengthen domestic resource mobilisation. It sits under the Plan d'orientation stratégique de l'administration fiscale (POSAF), itself built on the recommendations of the TADAT (2021) and PEFA assessments, and works on three lines: better exploitation of tax data, including automated cross-matching and analysis of information from the DGI and partner administrations (customs, treasury, budget); extension of digitalised tax procedures, notably connecting the **29 tax centres** not yet on SIGIBé, plus electronic document management with probative-value archiving and a pre-filled tax return; and the performance, reliability and security of the DGI's information system, including operationalising its business-continuity and disaster-recovery plans.

Two figures the fiche states, both to be carried dated and attributed to it rather than as measured outcomes: a feasibility study puts the pre-filled return's potential at **331 billion FCFA a year** in additional domestic resources and a **40 percent** improvement in the TADAT score; and the information system's conformity with the Politique de sécurité des systèmes d'information de l'État béninois (PSSIE) is reported to have risen **from 30 percent to 81.6 percent**, with the remaining activities expected to add a further 6.8 points (as at 2026-08-20).
recipient_organisation: Direction générale des impôts du Bénin

title: China Eximbank provides RMB 496 million government concessional loan for Phase 1 of National Broadband Network Project (Linked to Project ID#91638)
description: On April 7, 2015, China Eximbank and the Government of Benin signed an RMB 496 million government concessional loan (GCL) agreement [CHINA EXIMBANK GCL NO.35 (2014) TOTAL NO.(538) No. 1420103052015110579] for Phase 1 of National Broadband Network Project. This loan, which is captured via Project ID#58955, carried the following terms: a 20-year maturity, a 7-year grace period, a 2% interest rate, a 0% default (penalty) interest rate, a 0.25% management fee, and a 0.25% commitment fee. The borrower agreed to deposit project-related revenues in a special account to facilitate repayment. The borrower was expected to use the proceeds of the loan to finance a commercial contract between Benin Telecom S.A. and Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd., which was signed on August 5, 2014.   The purpose of the project was to expand access to high-speed internet, a fiber optic cable, and 4G technology by rehabilitating a 1060 km fiber optic backbone network that runs from Cotonou to Malanville, constructing a 222 km metropolitan fiber optic loop in Cotonou and surrounding areas, and deploying a 974 km high speed fiber optic broadband network with IMS/MPLS core. The project had six components: 1. Reinforcement of 2000 km of fiber optic cable called the ‘National Backbone’. 2. Building a metro network in Cotonou, comprised of almost 24 km of fiber optic cable. 3. Building a FTTx access network by modernizing sub-distributors of 125 Multi-Service Access Nodes (MSAN). 4. Modernizing a 230 km fiber optic cable line. 5. Creating 30 new 4G base stations. 6. Creating another IP Multimedia Subsystem core network. This project also involved the installation of 48 IP/MPLS routers to extend the IP BTS network. Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. was the contractor responsible for implementation.   A formal groundbreaking ceremony for the project’s first phase was held on November 26, 2015. However, Phase 1 implementation did not commence until December 2016. title: Benin Power Compact \u2014 National Electricity Dispatch Activity (National Distribution Control Center)
description: MCC's $391M Benin Power Compact (signed September 2015, entered force June 2017, closed June 2023) included the National Electricity Dispatch Activity ($31.4M), which financed construction of a national electricity distribution dispatch and control center in Akassato, Abomey-Calavi. The center was inaugurated on 22 June 2023. This is the first national dispatch center in Benin, providing centralised supervisory monitoring and remote control of 41 substations across the national distribution grid. Functions include real-time grid supervision, remote switching, fault detection and dispatch — SCADA-type operational technology. The center connects to the national medium-voltage network to reduce outages, improve reliability, and enable smarter grid management. This was part of the Electricity Distribution Project, alongside the Cotonou Grid Strengthening Activity ($145.3M) and Regional Grid Strengthening Activity ($80.6M).
